decidedBy: Essenthos, 2026-09-13, on the project owner's reading report of Genesis 2-4 and 10, each occurrence decided from the Hebrew and not from how a translation prints it
policy: An annotation says that a word is a name, and whose. Where the Hebrew is the common noun the word is not annotated however a translation prints it: הָאָדָם with the article is 'the man', and the King James printing Adam or the Synodal printing Адам does not make it the name. Where the Hebrew is the name and a lexeme-level marking or a missing reading left it unnamed or put it on the wrong record, the occurrence is ruled here, with the reason.
source: Essenthos, on the project owner's reading report of 2026-09-13, each occurrence decided from the Hebrew

rulings.why: The second אָדָם of the verse, וּלְאָדָם, is pointed without the article, where every mention from 2:19 to 2:23 is הָאָדָם, 'the man'. The Masoretic pointing reads the proper name here. Many modern translations emend to 'for the man', which is a reading against the text this corpus holds; the Synodal itself prints человека.

וּלְאָדָם אָמַר is pointed without the article, against הָאָדָם in 3:8-12, and the lexicon numbers the word H121, the name. The pointing is disputed — 'to the man' supposes a lost article — but read as the Masoretes pointed it, God speaks to Adam, as the King James and the Synodal both print it.
לְאָדָם וּלְאִשְׁתּוֹ is pointed without the article, beside הָאָדָם in 3:20 and 3:22. As in 2:20 and 3:17 the Masoretic pointing reads the name, and the King James prints it.
